headline: The only pending template pairs are six .svelte-only fixes (five Open WebUI, one Fava); a fresh CWE search found no new in-scope pairs. The highest-value, evidence-backed gap is Flask's extension-based Jinja autoescape: .jinja/.jinja2/.j2 templates are not autoescaped by Flask, while the template analyzer assumes they are (GHSA-pwgc in the suite). A naive {@html}/v-html hotspot would false-alarm on the fixed Svelte code, which keeps the sink and adds DOMPurify; Svelte needs a sanitizer-aware rule, not a bare hotspot.

gaps.evidence: GHSA-pwgc-w4x9-gw67 (changedetection.io) is in cve-pairs-python-frontend: the fix renames .jinja templates to .html because Flask only autoescapes .html/.htm/.xml/.xhtml; the current template analyzer treats .jinja/.jinja2/.j2 as autoescaping and only collects |safe/autoescape-off variables.
gaps.proposal: in core/analyzers/template_sinks.py, treat every {{ ... }} in a non-autoescaped extension (.jinja, .jinja2, .j2) as unescaped when the render call is Flask's render_template/render_template_string; keep the current |safe/autoescape-off model for Django's render/TemplateResponse, which autoescape their Jinja backend by default.
gaps.test: Flask view renders templates/page.jinja with {{ name }} from request.args -> vulnerable at the render call; templates/page.html -> safe; page.jinja with {{ name|e }} -> safe; Django render of a .jinja template -> safe.
gaps.risk: a framework-blind rule would false-alarm on Django's Jinja backend; the render call name must select the variant. Start as a review hotspot.

gaps.evidence: Six .svelte-only fixes are pending (open-webui, fava); .vue is a scored extension but no analyzer parses it. The fixes often keep {@html} or v-html with DOMPurify.sanitize, so a bare hotspot flags the fixed code too.
gaps.proposal: add .svelte to SOURCE_EXTENSIONS['python-web']; add a Svelte/Vue HTML rule that follows the expression back to a sanitizer (DOMPurify.sanitize, xss, escapeHtml) and treats v-html/{@html} of a literal as safe. Do not add a bare {@html} hotspot: the fixed Open WebUI files keep {@html html} after sanitizing.
gaps.test: vulnerable: {@html error} / {@html `${token.text}`}; safe: {@html DOMPurify.sanitize(x)} / v-html="trustedConstant". Score the six pending pairs only after this exists.
gaps.risk: without dataflow this is noisy; .svelte is not native Semgrep, so this may need a generic/pattern pre-pass.

gaps.evidence: mark_safe/Markup is the Python equivalent of a raw-HTML sink and is not in the XSS rule's sinks; no front-end suite case yet, but it is common in apps.
gaps.proposal: add mark_safe(...), markupsafe.Markup(...), django.utils.safestring.mark_safe(...) and flask.Markup(...) as sinks of codewatch.python.web.xss.
gaps.test: vulnerable: return mark_safe(request.args['x']); safe: mark_safe('fixed') or mark_safe(escape(x)).
gaps.risk: only tainted values; constants are common and stay safe.

gaps.evidence: GHSA-jxgr-gcj5-cqqg (Nautobot): filter values from the query string printed into unquoted data-* attributes and rebuilt by JS; the template rule only looks for |safe/autoescape off.
gaps.proposal: add a template hotspot for {{ ... }} inside an unquoted attribute (data-x={{ value }}); quoted attributes are already escaped by Jinja/Django.
gaps.test: vulnerable: <div data-name={{ name }}>; safe: <div data-name="{{ name }}"> (autoescaped) and constants.
gaps.risk: unquoted attributes are legal and often safe with constants; require a template expression, not a literal.

gaps.evidence: GHSA-xv64-8p4r-94gq (pgAdmin): '{{ layout }}' in a Jinja-rendered .js file; HTML autoescaping is not JS-string escaping, the fix uses |tojson. The template analyzer reads .html/.jinja but not .js.
gaps.proposal: flag {{ ... }} inside a JS string in files known to be Jinja-rendered (under templates/, or named by a render_template call), suggesting |tojson; do not treat every .js {{ }} as Jinja (Vue/Angular/Handlebars use it too).
gaps.test: vulnerable: var layout = '{{ layout }}'; safe: var layout = {{ layout|tojson }}; a Vue template with {{ msg }} is not a match.
gaps.risk: knowing which .js files Jinja renders is the hard part; keep it a hotspot and only for templates/.

gaps.evidence: no non-blind front-end case yet; React Router/Next/Vue/Angular/Svelte route and query hooks are not sources, so a DOM XSS through useSearchParams()/useRoute().query is missed.
gaps.proposal: after a non-blind case: add useSearchParams()[0].get, useParams(), useLocation().search/hash, next/navigation useSearchParams and the server searchParams prop, Vue useRoute().query/params/hash, Angular ActivatedRoute.snapshot.queryParams/params, Svelte $page.url.searchParams.
gaps.test: a React page rendering useSearchParams().get('q') into innerHTML; safe: textContent or an escaping helper.
gaps.risk: route params are often safe; taint only flags those reaching an HTML sink. Do not add without a case.

gaps.evidence: newer APIs are not in the sink list; no suite case yet.
gaps.proposal: add setHTMLUnsafe, document.parseHTMLUnsafe, Range.createContextualFragment and iframe.srcdoc as sinks; setHTML is the sanitizing API and stays safe.
gaps.test: vulnerable: el.setHTMLUnsafe(location.hash); safe: el.setHTML(sanitized) and textContent.
gaps.risk: low; these APIs are still uncommon.

gaps.evidence: the Python XSS rule treats request.path as a source; the JS rule stops at hash/search/href. A page that reflects location.pathname into HTML can be XSS.
gaps.proposal: add location.pathname/window.location.pathname/document.location.pathname as sources, with the same caution as the Python request.path source.
gaps.test: a page that writes location.pathname into innerHTML; safe: textContent.
gaps.risk: self-reflected paths are often harmless; only a sink decides.

gaps.evidence: pug/ejs/handlebars/nunjucks/mustache/eta are treated as escaping only for fixed literal templates; doT, lodash/underscore templates, hogan, dust, marko and squirrelly are not modelled.
gaps.proposal: research each engine's escaping semantics before adding: lodash/underscore <%= %> is raw while <%- %> escapes, unlike EJS; a wrong entry creates false negatives.
gaps.test: per engine, a fixed template printing a request value, plus a raw-output variant.
gaps.risk: engine-specific; do not add as a group.

gaps.evidence: the template rule is built at scan time and has no catalogue entry/CWE (PLAN step 26); the scorer derives the XSS CWEs, but the finding page has no title or CWE.
gaps.proposal: give codewatch.python.web.template.xss and codewatch.templates.unescaped-output a catalogue entry with the XSS metadata.
gaps.test: the catalogue lists the rule with CWE-79 and a title; the finding page shows it.

recommended_order: 1. Read the first nightly's 27-pair per-case table before changing front-end rules.
2. Fix the Flask .jinja/.jinja2/.j2 autoescape model in template_sinks.py; it is evidence-backed by GHSA-pwgc and needs a framework-aware test.
3. Add the evidence-backed sinks: jQuery HTML construction/dialog options (GHSA-x7mf, GHSA-fmqq), then React dangerouslySetInnerHTML and Python mark_safe/Markup.
4. Consider the unquoted-attribute and .js-Jinja hotspots; both are real but need local app checks for false alarms.
5. Build a Svelte/Vue rule and add .svelte scoring only if the six pending pairs matter; do not add a bare {@html} hotspot.
6. Defer client-route sources and new engine entries until a non-blind case exists.
caveats: No new in-scope pairs were found by the widened OSV search; the six .svelte cases are the only known pending set.
The .svelte fixes often keep {@html} with DOMPurify.sanitize, so a pattern hotspot would also fire on the fix and count as a false alarm; a dataflow/sanitizer-aware rule is required.
The two Open WebUI iframe cases are CWE-1021 (allow-same-origin), not HTML-injection sinks; a Svelte {@html} rule would not catch them.
.vue is in SOURCE_EXTENSIONS but no analyzer parses Vue templates; a future .vue-only pair would be scored as missed.

The Flask autoescape fix must distinguish Flask render_template calls from Django render calls: Django's Jinja backend autoescapes .jinja, Flask does not. A framework-blind rule would false-alarm on Django.
The front-end suite is not held out; the blind front-end suites must not be used to tune these rules.
